original:
Use case: identity-preserve. Make a production GAME SPRITE ATLAS for the SAME scruffy medieval player as the attached approved game art, in his earlier poor-villager stage. This is NOT a concept poster. Reference is the actual established knight walk: preserve its wiry thin adult proportions, slight forward stoop, ink weight, fine irregular carved hatch marks, aged warm off-white opaque material interiors, shabby Monty Python absurdity, sparse dirty muted orange. No glossy shading, realistic painting, blur, white halos, cute Disney faces, gigantic nose.
Output exactly 2048 wide x 1536 high, transparent RGBA, a strict 4 columns x 3 rows of 512x512 cells. Each complete figure entirely within its cell, centered with hips at x256, grounded boots at y480, crown around y40. No ground or ground shadows, labels, lines, grids, checkerboard, text, numbers. Truly transparent outside all figures.
One identical thin adult male with short messy dark hair, stubble, modest short crooked nose, small eyes hidden in narrow black brow shadows with one tiny ivory glint. Dirty pale cloth knee-length belted tunic, tiny faded orange patched collar and hem, narrow leggings and shabby rounded leather shoes. No heraldic badge on the villager. Same garment pattern and same identity/proportions across ALL twelve frames.
Each row is a FOUR KEY POSE SIDE PROFILE WALK CYCLE facing RIGHT, same camera. Column1 near leg ahead/far leg back, both boots touch ground; column2 near leg planted underneath hip, far knee flexed swinging forward; column3 far leg ahead/near leg back both boots touch ground; column4 far leg planted underneath hip, near knee flexed swinging forward. FEET ALWAYS POINT RIGHT along direction of travel, never toward viewer. Subtle weight down on contacts and rise in passing, torso/head counter movement; no legs swapping origin or crossing anatomically. Full body no cropping. Match gait pose position for corresponding columns in each row.
ROW1: truly unequipped villager: bare head, cloth sleeves, empty curled fists, no weapon, helmet, shield or metal armor. Hands held loosely near waist.
ROW2: EXACT SAME villager, same outfits face gait, now holds a short shabby straight sword in his near hand low across front, pointing right/down, other hand empty. Still NO armor/helmet/shield.
ROW3: EXACT SAME villager with battered cylindrical CLOSED bucket helmet exactly like the approved knight, tattered muted orange tabard with the same simple black cross, metal elbow guards, knee caps and greaves over cloth. Empty metal-gloved hands, NO sword or shield (armor-only upgrade). A full iron greathelm, closed, dark eye slit. Same poses as corresponding columns.
Do not add narrative scenery or UI. This sprite sheet is for immediate integration in a transparent 2D game and must have precise separate cell spacing, coherent anatomy and a restrained worn medieval woodcut aesthetic matching the source.
correction: Precise local costume correction to this exact sprite atlas. Preserve the 4 columns by 3 rows and every pose, face, body position, hairstyle, palette, scale, fine woodcut linework and transparent canvas. Change ONLY the legs in the TOP TWO ROWS: they are an unequipped peasant and must have plain worn fabric leggings, patched cloth knees and simple soft leather shoes. Remove all round metal kneecaps, metal shin armor, iron ankle bands and armor plates from those eight figures. Their knees must be cloth folds/patches rather than round armor cups. Keep the sword in the middle row, keep empty hands and bare head in the top row. BOTTOM ROW MUST REMAIN UNCHANGED: it is the armored upgrade with closed bucket helmets and orange cross tabards. Transparent outside, opaque parchment interiors, clean ink silhouettes, no added text or scenery, no colored edge fringe. This is a correction of the existing atlas, not a redesign.
tavern: Precise edit to the supplied FIRST PERSON tavern illustration: change ONLY the two player forearms/hands in the lower left and lower right. The player is a poor medieval peasant without any equipment. Replace all metal gauntlets, chainmail and orange armored sleeves with bare ordinary adult hands, plain dirty pale cloth tunic sleeves, a tiny dull orange seam accent. Keep the hands resting solidly in exactly the same positions on the table. Preserve the exact tavern room, beams, window, doorway, stool, tabletop edges, wood grain, bowl/spoon, mug, composition, size, warm light parchment and black engraved woodblock hatching. No figures across table. NO extra objects, no UI, no words, no gradients, no glossy shading. Match original line weight. Everything except the two foreground forearms/hands remains visually identical.
